objectives: Say what photosynthesis is and where it happens.
Write the word equation (and the symbol equation).
Name what goes in (reactants) and what comes out (products).
Describe how light, carbon dioxide and temperature change the rate.

keyVocabulary.meaning: how a plant makes its own food (glucose) using light energy
the green pigment that absorbs (traps) light energy
the part of a plant cell where photosynthesis happens
the sugar the plant makes; used for energy and growth
what you start with: carbon dioxide and water
what is made: glucose and oxygen
tiny holes under the leaf that let gases in and out
the thing in shortest supply that slows the rate down

explain: Plants cannot move to find food, so they make their own. They do this using light energy from the Sun.
Light energy is trapped by chlorophyll, the green pigment inside chloroplasts. The energy is used to join carbon dioxide (from the air) and water (from the soil) together.
This makes glucose, a sugar the plant uses for energy and growth. Oxygen is made as well and is released into the air.
wordEquation: carbon dioxide + water  →(light + chlorophyll)→  glucose + oxygen
glucoseUses: Released in respiration to give the plant energy.
Used to make new cells for growth.
Turned into cellulose to build strong cell walls.

limitingFactors: Light intensity — more light means a faster rate, until something else runs short.
Carbon dioxide — more CO₂ means a faster rate, up to a point.
Temperature — warmth speeds it up, but too hot damages the enzymes and it slows down.
commonMistakes: Mixing up the gases. A plant takes IN carbon dioxide and gives OUT oxygen — not the other way round.
Calling light a 'raw material'. The raw materials are water and carbon dioxide; light is the energy source.
Saying it happens 'in the leaf'. Be exact: it happens in the chloroplast inside the leaf cell.
Forgetting plants respire too. Plants photosynthesise AND respire (respiration never stops, day or night).
Writing the equation back to front. Reactants (CO₂ + water) are on the LEFT, products (glucose + oxygen) on the RIGHT.

content.title: Remember (content)
lines: IN: carbon dioxide + water.   OUT: glucose + oxygen.
Where: chloroplasts in the leaf.   Energy from: light, trapped by chlorophyll.
Plants photosynthesise AND respire — respiration never stops.

method.title: How to answer an 'explain' question
lines: 2  Say WHY using a key word (light / chlorophyll / chloroplast / rate).
3  Link it back to the question (so... / this means...).
Example: 'No light, so chlorophyll cannot trap energy, so no glucose is made.'

answers.title: Teacher answer key
rows: Q4: carbon dioxide + water → glucose + oxygen (light + chlorophyll above the arrow).
Q5: Any two of: respiration/energy, growth, stored as starch, made into cellulose.
Q6: No light energy, so chlorophyll cannot trap energy; without light the reaction cannot run, so no glucose is made.
Q7: More light = more energy = faster rate, so more oxygen made. It stops increasing when another factor becomes limiting (carbon dioxide, temperature) or light is no longer the limiting factor.
